exposure: Ambient particulate matter with diameter <2.5 µm (PM2.5) levels at maternal residential address (each trimester and the month preceding delivery)
cohort: The study included neonates born in Massachusetts between 2001 and 2015, whose data was retrieved from the Massachusetts birth registry.
finding: Prenatal exposure to PM2.5 in late pregnancy reduced gestational age at delivery among Massachusetts neonates, with a more pronounced effect on preterm/early-term births, male neonates, and neonates of younger and African American mothers.
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery was a primary outcome and was analyzed at 2.5th, 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 97.5th percentiles.
